purpose: Machine-readable map of defaults, exceptions and where each capability belongs.
principles: The engine is domain-neutral: it knows resources, fields, scopes, queries and presentation metadata, never brands, cars, states or airports.
Defaults are safe and bounded; a consumer declares only an exception or an ambiguous relationship.
Tenant scope is server-owned and mandatory for tenant data. Global scope is explicit, read-only and never inferred from a table name.
The browser may choose values and search text, but never a tenant, table, column, SQL statement, adapter or lookup target.
Reference data is stored once, cached by the server and queried by dependency; never copied once per tenant or preloaded in full by every user.
workflow: Read capability-map.md to distinguish published behavior from planned backlog items.
Classify the resource as tenant data or explicit global reference data.
Start with the automatic registration and inspect the generated definition.
Add a typed option only when the default is not correct for this resource.
For dependent lookups, register each target resource and declare only the dependency field keys.
Run the smoke test for the setting group and verify tenant isolation, read-only global behavior and bounded requests.

settings.whenToUse: All tenant-owned records in a SaaS product.
settings.security: The ScopeProvider supplies tenant_id; the HTTP request cannot override it.

settings.whenToUse: Immutable or centrally managed catalogs shared by tenants, such as FIPE or postal geography.
settings.security: Must be explicit and read-only; never add tenant_id just to duplicate global rows.

settings.whenToUse: The valid options of one field depend on values already chosen in the form.
settings.engineBehavior: Server validates dependencies, clears downstream draft values, transports depends.<field>, applies scope and pages the target resource.

settings.whenToUse: Always for repeated lookup reads; use a shared implementation when the service has multiple instances.
settings.engineBehavior: Key includes target resource, value/label fields, search, cursor, fixed filters, declared dependencies and trusted scope; global resources share entries across tenants, tenant resources do not.

settings.whenToUse: Large catalogs where searching with one or two characters would create noisy, expensive requests; set a smaller value only when the catalog's identifiers require it.
settings.engineBehavior: The renderer does not issue filtered lookup requests until the typed value reaches the configured minimum. The explicit options control still loads the bounded initial page.

settings.whenToUse: Partition one generic auxiliary table into server-defined catalogs such as kind=state or kind=currency.
settings.engineBehavior: A server-owned typed value list combines with declared dependencies, trusted scope, archive and the lookup cache. One value applies equality; multiple values apply membership. If the lookup must expose one catalog, declare one catalog ID; multiple IDs intentionally expose their union. It is never accepted from the browser and never replaces tenant scope or authorization.

settings.whenToUse: The operator needs a different subset or order than the automatic projection.

settings.default: all visible writable fields in definition order
settings.whenToUse: The form needs an intentional order or a smaller writable projection.
Only when the schema and business rule explicitly permit an empty value.
Use a static scalar that should prefill a new form and be applied when a create mutation omits the field. Dynamic expressions remain adapter-owned.
settings.engineBehavior: The renderer pre-populates create forms and the core applies the same value only during create normalization; updates never replace an existing value.

settings.whenToUse: The schema or business rule has a smaller or otherwise explicit finite bound.

settings.declaration: Field.Pattern or sqladapter.WithPattern; prefer public crud.Pattern* constants for common shapes
settings.whenToUse: A field needs a reusable format constraint such as a code, acronym, identifier, Unicode letter shape or controlled textual value.
settings.engineBehavior: The server compiles the RE2 expression during bootstrap and applies it during create/update validation. PatternMessage is a localizable message code; the browser never supplies the expression. Presets are readable string constants; custom RE2 remains available for reviewed cases.

settings.whenToUse: The desktop interaction should be explicitly select, radio, segmented or buttons; mobile may force native select.

settings.default: discover finite CHECK/enum metadata at bootstrap
settings.whenToUse: Use WithEnum only when the adapter cannot expose structural values or labels need an explicit consumer mapping.

settings.declaration: sqladapter.RegisterReadModel with ReadModelConfig and ReadOnly fields
settings.whenToUse: Use when a grid needs a value supplied by a registered join or calculation; keep the field out of mutations and leave query execution to the adapter.
settings.engineBehavior: The core exposes adapter-returned read-only fields, validates registered filter/sort allowlists and rejects attempts to write them. When SQL aliases equal public field keys, the SQL adapter infers field/scope maps and searchable/sortable allowlists from the definition; explicit maps remain available for aliases or narrower projections. The server-owned query is validated once at bootstrap; SQL and join syntax never come from HTTP.

settings.whenToUse: A screen or smoke test needs a smaller declared page size; the service remains bounded.
Enable a server-declared Excluídos toggle when operators must consult archived records together with active records.
settings.engineBehavior: The browser can request include_archived only when the registered Grid declares active_and_archived. Adapters return Archived metadata; the renderer marks those rows with an Excluído badge in the actions column, a dedicated visual rail and hides edit/delete actions. Restoration is a separate capability.

settings.whenToUse: The product explicitly chooses recoverable archive semantics; otherwise no delete action is exposed.
Only when physical deletion is an explicit, reviewed product policy; it is mutually exclusive with archive.

notEngineSettings: FIPE, Correios, airline, airport or other domain catalogs and their import schedules
tenant selection supplied by a browser
workflow, approval, payments, documents or external side effects
